title_en: Jingwei Textile Machinery Co., Ltd. v. Qiu Yafen et al. — dispute over an installment sales contract
ruling_gist_en: Among multiple debtors determined by an effective judgment, if only some of the debtors apply for retrial and their reasons are meritorious, the people's court, when ruling to retry the case in accordance with the law, shall also examine whether the retrial may affect the other debtors' assumption of debts under the original judgment. If the retrial does not affect the other debtors' assumption of debts under the original judgment, the court shall only stay the enforcement against the applicant for retrial, so as to ensure that while realizing the function of correcting errors through retrial according to law, the legitimate rights and interests of creditors are reasonably protected.

full_text_en:
Jingwei Textile Machinery Co., Ltd. v. Qiu Yafen et al. — Dispute over Installment Sales Contract

Ruling Summary

If, among multiple debtors determined in an effective judgment, only some debtors apply for retrial and their reasons are valid, the people's court, when ruling to retry the case in accordance with law, shall also examine whether the retrial of the case may affect other debtors' performance of debts in accordance with the original judgment. If the retrial does not affect other debtors' performance of debts in accordance with the original judgment, execution shall be stayed only against the retrial applicant, so as to reasonably protect the lawful rights and interests of the creditor while achieving the function of correcting errors through retrial in accordance with law.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Shen Zi No. 1823

Retrial Applicant (First-instance Defendant): Qiu Yafen, female, Han ethnicity, born on February 9, 1964, residing in Shaoxing City, Zhejiang Province, currently residing in Shihezi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Respondent (First-instance Plaintiff): Jingwei Textile Machinery Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 8 Yongchang Middle Road, Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Ye Maoxin, Chairman of the Company.

First-instance Defendant: Xinjiang Tiansheng Industrial Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 87-95, Development Zone, Shihezi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Zhang Xinghai, Manager of the Company.

First-instance Defendant: Xiongfeng Holding Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: Fuquan Town, Shaoxing County, Zhejiang Province.

Legal Representative: He Xingrong, Chairman of the Company.

First-instance Defendant: Zhang Xinghai, male, Han ethnicity, born on September 16, 1957, residing in Shaoxing County, Zhejiang Province.

First-instance Defendant: He Xingrong, male, Han ethnicity, born on August 28, 1964, residing in Shaoxing County, Zhejiang Province.

First-instance Defendant: Chen Yali, female, Han ethnicity, born on March 24, 1963, residing in Shaoxing County, Zhejiang Province.

First-instance Defendant: Ge Shuiguo, male, Han ethnicity, born on September 28, 1966, residing in Shaoxing County, Zhejiang Province.

Agent ad litem: Yang Yunfeng, lawyer of Xinjiang Shuangxin Law Firm.

First-instance Defendant: Tang Peifang, female, Han ethnicity, born on March 21, 1970, residing in Shaoxing County, Zhejiang Province.

The retrial applicant, Qiu Yafen, due to dissatisfaction with the civil judgment (2012) Xin Bing Min Er Chu Zi No. 00008 rendered by the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region in the case of dispute over installment sales contract with the respondent, Jingwei Textile Machinery Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jingwei Company), and the first-instance defendants, Xinjiang Tiansheng Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tiansheng Company), Xiongfeng Holding Group Co., Ltd., Zhang Xinghai, He Xingrong, Chen Yali, Ge Shuiguo, and Tang Peifang, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to examine this case, and the examination has now been concluded.

Qiu Yafen applied for retrial on the following grounds: (I) The first-instance proceedings of this case were illegal. First, according to the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the complaint filed by Jingwei Company should state the parties' occupations, work units, evidence and sources of evidence, but the complaint lacked all the above content, which did not meet the conditions for case filing and acceptance. Second, the first-instance court used service by publication when Jingwei Company did not state Qiu Yafen's work unit and there was no evidence showing that Qiu Yafen's whereabouts were unknown, which violated the provisions of Article 92 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. Third, the first-instance court deprived Qiu Yafen of her procedural right to request expert evaluation and did not order expert evaluation of the Personal Guarantee Letter which contained significant doubts. (II) The facts found in this case were erroneous. First, in the first-instance judgment, there was no evidence proving that Jingwei Company paid RMB 76.8 million to Tiansheng Company. Second, Qiu Yafen's signature on the Personal Guarantee Letter was forged and should not be admitted as evidence. Qiu Yafen applied for retrial pursuant to Items (2) and (8) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

This Court found upon examination that the case file of (2012) Xin Bing Min Er Chu Zi No. 00008 did not contain any record that the first-instance court had used other methods of service before serving the litigation documents on Qiu Yafen by publication, and there was no evidence showing that Qiu Yafen's whereabouts were unknown during the first-instance proceedings, and Qiu Yafen did not attend the first-instance trial.

This Court holds that the facts found above are sufficient to determine that the first-instance court violated the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 92 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, which states that "service by publication shall be used if the person on whom the document is to be served is unknown in whereabouts, or if service cannot be effected by any other means provided in this Section," and the second paragraph of the same Article, which states that "the reasons and process of service by publication shall be recorded in the case file." Qiu Yafen's grounds for retrial meet the circumstances specified in Item (8) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and this case shall be retried.

Article 405 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides: "When trying a retrial case, the people's court shall focus on the retrial claims." Qiu Yafen's retrial claim is to dismiss Jingwei Company's claim for her to bear guarantee liability. The grounds relied upon are: first, Jingwei Company did not pay RMB 76.8 million to Tiansheng Company, i.e., the principal claim and debt did not exist; second, Qiu Yafen's signature on the Personal Guarantee Letter was a forgery. Regarding the first ground, the first-instance court found that Jingwei Company submitted the Cotton Purchase and Sale Contract signed by both parties, which stated that Jingwei Company purchased ginned cotton from Tiansheng Company, with payment before delivery, and the initial payment was RMB 76.8 million. After the contract was signed, Tiansheng Company issued to Jingwei Company the Confirmation Letter on Inability to Perform the Cotton Purchase and Sale Contract, stating that "Your company had paid RMB 76.8 million of the purchase price on December 17, 2010." Tiansheng Company also issued the Repayment Commitment Letter, stating that "Your company's RMB 76.8 million has still not been repaid to date." The debtor Tiansheng Company also confirmed receipt of that amount. Based on the parties' statements and the above evidence verified through trial, the first-instance court found that Jingwei Company had paid RMB 76.8 million to Tiansheng Company. Qiu Yafen now denies that the principal claim and debt actually occurred, but she failed to submit relevant evidence and cannot overturn the above finding of the first-instance court. This ground cannot be established and should not be included in the scope of retrial. Regarding the second ground, because the first-instance court's service by publication violated the provisions of Article 92 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, Qiu Yafen was unable to attend the first-instance trial, was unable to cross-examine the Personal Guarantee Letter, and was also unable to exercise her right to request expert evaluation. Therefore, whether Qiu Yafen's reason that her signature on the Personal Guarantee Letter was a forgery and her claim that she should not bear guarantee liability on that basis can be established shall be determined by the retrial court based on the facts and law while lawfully safeguarding Qiu Yafen's litigation rights. Accordingly, the retrial of this case shall focus on whether Qiu Yafen's signature on the Personal Guarantee Letter was forged and whether Qiu Yafen should bear guarantee liability.

After the first-instance judgment was rendered, except for Qiu Yafen, the principal debtor Tiansheng Company and the other guarantors did not appeal and did not apply for retrial. To lawfully protect the rights of the creditor, Jingwei Company, in accordance with the provisions of Article 206 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, which states that "For a case decided to be retried under the trial supervision procedure, execution of the original judgment, ruling or mediation document shall be suspended by ruling, except for cases involving claims for alimony, support for children or elders, maintenance, pension for the disabled or the family of the deceased, medical expenses, labor remuneration, etc., for which execution may not be suspended," execution is stayed only against Qiu Yafen in this case, and execution against Tiansheng Company and the other guarantors is not stayed.

In conclusion, Qiu Yafen's application for retrial meets the circumstances specified in Item (8) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. Pursuant to Articles 204 and 206 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

1. The Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region is hereby directed to retry this case;

2. During the retrial, execution against Qiu Yafen is stayed.

Presiding Judge: Lin Wenxue

Judge: Liu Xiaofei

Acting Judge: Ye Yang

November 20, 2015

Clerk: Wei Ran

[Introduction of the Presiding Judge]

Lin Wenxue, Senior Judge, born in 1970, Doctor of Laws, appointed as Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2007.
